paragraphs: Storm Boelo is coming to Ireland today, Saturday. Met Éireann has orange warnings for the west.
There is an orange rain warning for Galway and Kerry. It is from 7am to 2pm today. Very heavy rain may cause floods.
There is also an orange wind warning for Donegal, Galway, Leitrim, Mayo and Sligo. It starts at 2pm today and ends at 9am on Sunday. Strong winds may knock down trees and power lines.
Yellow warnings cover many other counties, like Clare, Cork, Limerick, Cavan and Monaghan.
Stay away from the sea and rivers. Do not walk or drive through floodwater. Do not touch fallen wires. Tie down things in your garden.
Storm Boelo is bringing very heavy rain and strong winds to Ireland today, only days after Storm Austen. Met Éireann has issued orange warnings for parts of the west and north-west.

An orange rain warning is in place for Galway and Kerry from 7am until 2pm on Saturday. A yellow rain warning covers Clare, Cork, Donegal, Galway, Kerry, Leitrim, Limerick, Mayo and Sligo from 4am to 3pm. The ground is already very wet after Storm Austen, so rivers may rise quickly and cause flooding.

An orange wind warning for Donegal, Galway, Leitrim, Mayo and Sligo begins at 2pm on Saturday and ends at 9am on Sunday. There will be very strong winds with dangerous gusts. Trees may fall, power may go off, and big waves may flood coastal areas. Yellow wind warnings cover Connacht, Clare, Kerry, Limerick, Cavan and Monaghan until Sunday.
Travel by road, rail, air and ferry may be disrupted. More rain is expected on Monday, the bank holiday.

The Coast Guard tells people near the sea to "stay back, stay high, stay dry". Never walk or drive through floodwater. Do not go near fallen power lines, and report them to the ESB on 1800 372 999. Tie down garden furniture, charge your phone and check on older neighbours.

Storm Boelo is sweeping in from the Atlantic today, bringing very heavy rain and damaging winds only days after Storm Austen. Met Éireann has issued Status Orange warnings for several counties in the west and north-west.

An orange rain warning is in force for Galway and Kerry from 7am to 2pm on Saturday, with a yellow rain warning for Clare, Cork, Donegal, Galway, Kerry, Leitrim, Limerick, Mayo and Sligo from 4am to 3pm. Because the ground is already saturated, rivers could rise rapidly, leading to flooding of roads, homes and businesses.

A Status Orange wind warning for Donegal, Galway, Leitrim, Mayo and Sligo runs from 2pm on Saturday until 9am on Sunday, with gale-force westerly winds and severe gusts expected to peak on Saturday evening. Power cuts, fallen trees and coastal flooding are likely, and storm force 10 winds are possible at sea. Yellow wind warnings also apply to Connacht, Clare, Kerry, Limerick, Cavan and Monaghan.
Disruption to flights, ferries, trains and buses is possible. Another low-pressure system is expected to bring more rain on the Monday bank holiday, while spring tides could worsen coastal flooding.

The Coast Guard urges people to "stay back, stay high, stay dry". Do not walk or drive through floodwater: just 15cm of fast-moving water can knock a person over. Keep away from fallen wires and report them to the ESB on 1800 372 999. Secure loose outdoor items, charge your phone and check on vulnerable neighbours.

Storm Boelo is barrelling in from the Atlantic today, unleashing torrential rain and destructive gusts hard on the heels of Storm Austen. Met Éireann has escalated to Status Orange warnings across swathes of the west and north-west.

An orange rain warning is in force for Galway and Kerry between 7am and 2pm on Saturday, underpinned by a yellow alert for Clare, Cork, Donegal, Galway, Kerry, Leitrim, Limerick, Mayo and Sligo from 4am to 3pm. With the ground already waterlogged, swift runoff could cause rivers to burst their banks and inundate roads and properties.

A Status Orange wind warning for Donegal, Galway, Leitrim, Mayo and Sligo is in effect from 2pm on Saturday until 9am on Sunday, with gale-force westerlies and ferocious gusts set to peak overnight. Outages, toppled trees and coastal inundation are anticipated, and storm force 10 is forecast offshore. Yellow wind alerts extend to Connacht, Clare, Kerry, Limerick, Cavan and Monaghan.

Air, sea, rail and bus services may be thrown into disarray. A fresh low-pressure system is poised to deliver further rain on the Monday bank holiday, and spring tides threaten to compound coastal flooding.

The Coast Guard implores the public to "stay back, stay high, stay dry". Never wade or drive through floodwater, as a mere 15cm of fast-flowing water can sweep a person off their feet. Steer clear of downed lines and report them to the ESB on 1800 372 999. Batten down loose outdoor items, keep phones charged and look in on vulnerable neighbours.
